merger_description:
IFM Fiduciary Pty Ltd (**IFM Fiduciary**) as trustee of the SSCF SOA8 Holding Trust, a wholly owned subsidiary of IFM Holdings Pty Ltd (**IFM Holdings**), proposes to acquire 75% of the issued share capital in Salads of Australia Pty Limited (Receivers & Managers Appointed) (Administrators Appointed) (**SOA**) from Tesswatt Investments Pty Ltd in its capacity as trustee of the Tesswatt Investment Trust by way of Share Purchase Deed (the **Acquisition**).

IFM Holdings, through its subsidiaries, is a global institutional investor and asset manager across infrastructure, debt investments, listed equities and private equity. It is owned by a collective of 15 Australian industry super funds and one UK pension fund and operates independently of its owners.

SOA, through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is the holding company of PM Fresh Pty Ltd (**PM Fresh**) and certain other subsidiaries, an Australian fresh salad manufacturer, operating a national network of production facilities with processing capabilities. The company specialises in wet (deli) salads, salad kits, salad bowls, salad leaf, value-added vegetables, and fresh snacking solutions.

determination_table_content.details:
IFM Fiduciary Pty Ltd (IFM Fiduciary) as trustee of the SSCF SOA8
Holding Trust, a wholly owned subsidiary of IFM Holdings Pty Ltd
(IFM Holdings), applied for a notification waiver in respect of its
proposed acquisition of 75% of the issued share capital in Salads of
Australia Pty Limited (Receivers & Managers Appointed)
(Administrators Appointed) (SOA) from Tesswatt Investments Pty
Ltd in its capacity as trustee of the Tesswatt Investment Trust
(Tesswatt) by way of Share Purchase Deed, as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, IFM Fiduciary, is a wholly owned subsidiary of IFM
Holdings. IFM Holdings, through its subsidiaries, is a global
institutional investor and asset manager across infrastructure, debt
investments, listed equities and private equity. It is owned by a
collective of 15 Australian industry super funds and one UK pension
fund and operates independently of its owners.
The target, SOA, through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is the holding
company of PMFresh Pty Ltd (PM Fresh) and certain other
subsidiaries, an Australian fresh salad manufacturer, operating a
national network of production facilities with processing capabilities.
The company specialises in wet (deli) salads, salad kits, salad bowls,
salad leaf, value-added vegetables, and fresh snacking solutions.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular, there is no horizontal overlap
or vertical relationships between IFM Fiduciary (or its connected
entities) and PM Fresh in the supply of salads and packaged fruit
and vegetable products in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
